Agent tools for Workspace ONE

An AI agent runs device management. A person approves the dangerous parts.

A personal project on the public Workspace ONE API. Not an Omnissa product.

ws1 CLI on GitHub ↗MCP server on GitHub ↗
How it works

A command-line tool and Claude skill that let an AI agent do routine work in Workspace ONE, the console IT teams use to manage company laptops and phones.

The hard part. An agent that can wipe a laptop must never do it alone. Destructive commands open a one-time approval page the agent can’t see or click, and every change lands in a tamper-evident log.

Built with. A Go CLI generated from 10 OpenAPI specs, shipped with a Claude skill. Anything missing from the policy file counts as destructive. An earlier MCP server with 21 tools is public too.

02 / 0521:00TestFlight

One of Them Is Lying

A detective game where every suspect is an AI on your phone.

  1. 01Pick a case
  2. 02Meet the suspects
  3. 03Question them in your own words
  4. 04Accuse the liar
  • 56cases
  • 2.8 sper answer, on the phone
  • Jul–Oct 2026
How it works

Question suspects in your own words, find the contradiction, and confront the one who’s lying. The AI runs on the iPhone itself, with no server.

The hard part. Small on-device models make poor liars: they drop the story or never confess. Each suspect now holds a written cover story, and the game decides when the right evidence breaks it.

Built with. SwiftUI on iOS 26 with Apple Foundation Models: one model session per suspect, with voice in and out. A content linter keeps cases separate from the engine, and a test suite plays every case’s solution against the real model.

03 / 0522:00Beta

Aloud

Dictation that never sends your voice anywhere.

TextEdit
Re: launch planHi Dana, thanks for the notes on the launch plan, let’s move the beta to the 12th and keep the pricing page as it is. I’ll send the new timeline tomorrow morning.

fnHold to talk · release to insert

  • 1key to hold
  • 3on-device speech engines
  • Jun–Sep 2026
How it works

Hold one key, speak, and clean text appears at your cursor in any Mac app. Recognition and cleanup both run on the Mac.

The hard part. Private has to be provable. Automated tests check for any outgoing network traffic, and IT can switch dictation history off across a fleet but can’t switch it on.

Built with. A Swift 6 menu-bar app. Parakeet, Parakeet Realtime and Whisper run on Core ML behind one protocol; cleanup uses Apple Foundation Models with a local Qwen3 fallback. 1,546 offline tests.

htmd on GitHub ↗
How it works

Turns an AI agent’s answer into an interactive page. There are 24 templates: a decision matrix, a kanban board, an approval list, a slide deck, a code review, a dashboard and more. The reader edits the page and sends the changes back as one prompt.

The hard part. An agent writing a whole web page is slow and costly. In htmd the agent writes a few lines of YAML and a template draws the page, with dark mode, print styles and drag and drop built in. The decision matrix here is about 360 tokens of YAML; the finished page is 9,000 to 12,000 tokens of HTML.

Built with. A Node 20 CLI and library that writes one self-contained HTML file, with an optional serve mode. MIT licensed.

The Token Desk on YouTube ↗
How it works

A production line for an AI explainer channel. It researches, writes, narrates, illustrates, captions and assembles each video. I pick the style, mark up the script, review the cut and publish.

The hard part. Early scripts sounded staged, with the narrator asking itself questions. I rebuilt the script stage around 3Blue1Brown’s teaching sequence, and a checker now flags those tells.

Built with. A Next.js console over a SQLite job queue and a background render worker. Claude writes every language step, GPT Image draws, narration runs on a local voice model, and Whisper and ffmpeg assemble each cut.
